CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain and swelling following a fall.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Stephanie Morales is a 36-year-old female presenting with left ankle pain and swelling that began two days ago. Patient reports slipping on snow and ice while walking to her car, causing her left ankle to turn underneath her. She fell to the ground and was able to get up afterward, though the ankle was very sore and began swelling significantly with considerable pain, making walking difficult. Patient has tried ibuprofen, ice, and elevation, which provided mild relief. Pain is localized to the outside of the ankle with no pain in the calf, lower leg, or knee. No bleeding noted, though swelling is present.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies pain above the ankle. Denies bleeding. Confirms swelling of the left ankle. No other systems reviewed in detail.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
2. Hypertension
3. Systolic ejection murmur (unchanged from prior)

MEDICATIONS
1. Metformin (for diabetes)
2. Norvasc (for hypertension) - refill requested

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient exercises and manages diet, particularly avoiding sweets and sugars. Patient is motivated to return to exercising.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Alert, appears uncomfortable with ankle injury
Neck: No bruits
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Heart: Normal rate and rhythm with 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (unchanged from prior), not of concern
Abdomen: Benign
Left ankle: Tenderness over lateral malleolus and fifth metatarsal, swelling, redness, pain with valgus stressing of ankle. Normal sensation and pulses distally.

RESULTS
X-ray of left ankle ordered pending results.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Left ankle sprain with possible fifth metatarsal fracture - order left ankle x-ray to rule out fracture. Place in air splint with crutches for non-weightbearing status pending imaging. If fracture confirmed, will refer to orthopedics. If no fracture, will advance to partial weightbearing. Prescribe naproxen 500 mg twice daily for pain control. Continue ice and elevation.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus - well controlled on current regimen with hemoglobin A1c of 6.8. Continue metformin. Order hemoglobin A1c and baseline labs today. Patient has ophthalmology appointment scheduled for diabetic eye exam in next couple of weeks. Patient counseled to continue current diet and exercise regimen.

3. Hypertension - controlled on current therapy with today's blood pressure 120/70. Refill norvasc. Continue monitoring and call if any changes.
